enrichment.summary: Aer Faber AS is a Spydeberg-based (Østfold, NO) manufacturer and distributor of ventilation components — circular and rectangular ducts, stainless hoods, grilles, transitions, silencers and spiro — with its own machine park, plus a stocked trade counter/shop selling fittings (Ø80–Ø1250), dampers, valves, insulation, sheet-metal tools and workwear (f2, f6, f7, f8). Since December 2020 the company has been owned by the Swedish listed Lindab Group, and it now operates as part of Lindab's Norwegian organisation while also reselling Lindab and other suppliers' products (f24, f23, f9). Revenue was ~€6.6M in 2025 with ~25 employees and strong reported margins (EBIT €1.1M).

score.why_now: On paper this looks like the perfect Nordic industrial target — €6.6M revenue, ~17% EBIT margin, 25 people, niche ventilation duct manufacturing with a stocked trade counter — but it isn't for sale by anyone we can call. Lindab (Swedish listed) bought Aer Faber in December 2020 and it now sits as one of four companies under Lindab A/S, with two Lindab group people on the board; the 'Erik Iversen, 45' in our row isn't corroborated anywhere (registry says Eirik Austad, local press says Geir Pettersen). There is no founder, no succession question and no majority owner to approach — any deal would be a carve-out decided in Malmö, and Lindab has given zero signal of divesting a unit local press calls a star performer. The real value of this record is inverted: Lindab is an active consolidator of Nordic ventilation and sheet-metal businesses and belongs in MGX as a buyer, not a seller. Park the sell-side outreach; route the entity to the buy-side team and keep the Østfold ventilation sector on the radar for genuinely owner-led targets.

enrichment.summary: Aquaservice AS is a Norwegian manufacturer of HDPE-based water-handling equipment for aquaculture and maritime industries, operating a 12,000 m² engineering and production facility in Straumgjerde, Sykkylven (f4, f9). Its product range spans self-cleaning industrial pressure filters, the design-protected Aquatrans three-way fish-transport valve, UV plants, pool treatment systems, sea pipelines, certified service rafts and HardRIB boats (f9, f20, f23, f8). Founded in 1985, the company passed through Ocea/Steinsvik/ScaleAQ ownership before key personnel bought it back in 2021, and it is now expanding internationally with units in the UK (2025) and Chile (2026) (f7, f3, f2, f5, f6).

score.why_now: Aquaservice is a classic Nordic niche engineering play: HDPE water-handling equipment with design-protected products (Aquatrans valve, self-cleaning Aquafilter), ISO 9001 since Dec 2025, and revenue up ~52% to NOK 47m (~€4M) in 2025 after a tax-uncertainty dip in 2024. The owners are a small group of key personnel who bought the business back from ScaleAQ in 2021 — five years in, with the growth case now proven and two international units (UK 2025, Chile 2026) burning working capital and management bandwidth, this is exactly the moment when a manager-owner group starts thinking about a second liquidity event or a strategic partner. The CEO is only 50 and in build-out mode, so this is not a succession story; the credible entry is growth capital or a minority stake to fund the UK/Chile expansion, with the Listed Nordic engineering group and the Nordic lower-mid-market PE fund as obvious counterparties — the sector's own consolidation history (Ocea → Steinsvik → ScaleAQ) makes the conversation natural. Caveat: at ~€4M revenue with no published EBITDA, the €3-5M floor is plausible but unproven, so qualify profitability on the first call.

enrichment.summary: Argus Remote Systems AS is a Bergen (Laksevåg) based designer and manufacturer of electric ROV (remotely operated vehicle) systems for subsea work, with nine ROV models spanning inspection-class to heavy work-class units rated to 7,000 m, plus its own Poseidon control system, tether management systems, LARS and DNV-certified control containers (f3, f5, f17, f18, f11). Over 164 complete ROV systems have been delivered in 30+ years, with customers in aquaculture, oil & gas, subsea power cable, defence and research (f3, f4, f26). The company reported 2025 revenue of €31.8M and EBIT of €6.2M with 48 employees, is 70% owned by Mohn Drilling and 30% by employees (f1).

score.why_now: Argus is a rare, profitable Norwegian subsea-robotics OEM — €31.8M revenue, €6.2M EBIT (~19%), proprietary Poseidon control software, 164 delivered ROV systems and a live order book across Shearwater, Mermaid, offshore wind and defence. The timing hook is the leadership transition: 67-year-old Frode Korneliussen appears to have stepped back to Senior Advisor with Renate Hvidevoll taking over as CEO, which is exactly the moment holding companies re-examine their position. The catch is the cap table — this is not a founder-owned situation: 70% sits with Mohn Drilling and 30% with employees, so the real conversation is with the Mohn owner group, not the CEO, and an industrial family holding can sit on an asset like this indefinitely. That said, subsea robotics is consolidating hard and our Nordic lower-mid-market PE fund, the Finnish evergreen family office and the listed Nordic engineering group would all move on this at the size and margin profile; even a partial/minority framing gives us a credible soft entry. Worth a well-researched 'open' approach to Mohn Drilling now, with the CEO handover as the natural pretext.

companies.industry: Produksjon av varer av metalltråd, kjetting og fjærer

products: Standard and project-specific welded reinforcement mesh (spesialnett, NS 3576-4, Kontrollrådet Class K)
enrichment.summary: 7 Steel Service Norway AS (formerly Celsa Steel Service) is a nationwide Norwegian supplier of reinforcement steel products for the construction and infrastructure sector, with cut-and-bend rebar, welded mesh, roll reinforcement (BAMTEC), prefabricated cages and rebar accessories, backed by value-added services such as rebar drawing, BIM/IFC-based ordering and mechanical testing. Rebar is supplied from a 100% scrap-based electric arc furnace steel mill in Mo i Rana (Mo Industripark) running on hydropower, which the company markets as Europe's cleanest rebar at 388 kg CO2e/tonne. It operates production, warehouses and sales offices from Kristiansand to Tromsø and reported NOK-equivalent €118.0M revenue in 2025 with 146 employees.

score.why_now: On paper this looks like a Nordic industrial champion — €118M revenue, 146 people, seven sites, the largest rebar processor in the Nordics with a genuinely differentiated low-carbon story that CBAM and the EU melt-and-pour rules from October 2026 make commercially valuable. But it is almost certainly not our deal: the Celsa Steel Service heritage and the rebrand to 7 Steel, plus the in-group EAF mill in Mo i Rana, point to a foreign steel group subsidiary, not a founder-owned business. Espen Marthinsen is 61 and the right age, but he is daglig leder, not visibly the majority owner, so the sale decision sits with a parent we haven't identified. Add a €1.2M EBIT on €118M of revenue with a €1.0M net loss, ongoing capex (new Trondheim factory, new Bergen/Ålesund premises), and a revenue scale that exceeds every mandate in our network except the logistics fund (wrong sector), and this becomes a carve-out conversation for a strategic steel/infrastructure buyer rather than a classic succession mandate. Worth 30 minutes of ownership verification via Brønnøysund shareholder data; if it turns out there is a Norwegian management-owned holding structure, it flips quickly — otherwise park it.

signals.note: Espen Marthinsen is 61, but tenure and whether he holds equity are unknown; if he is a hired group CEO the age signal carries no transaction weight.

signals.signal: Likely group subsidiary / carve-out, not founder-owned
signals.note: Rebrand from Celsa Steel Service to 7 Steel Service and reliance on an in-group Mo i Rana steel mill strongly suggest a foreign parent controls the decision — outside Mergero's ideal majority-owner profile.
FY2025 EBIT €1.2M (1% margin) and net result €-1.0M on €118M revenue; EBITDA not derivable. Value would hinge on normalised EBITDA and asset base, not an earnings multiple.
New Trondheim factory staffed up in 2023, new Bergen and Ålesund premises — an investment/expansion posture rather than a harvest posture.
€118M exceeds the revenue ceiling of every industrial mandate in the network (max €80M DACH, €60M listed Nordic engineering group); realistic buyers are steel strategics outside our current book.
388 kg CO2e/tonne scrap-based hydropower rebar, ~40% improved 2026 EPD — a credible equity story for a strategic or infrastructure buyer as imports get penalised from 2026/2027.

signals.signal: Blue-chip customer base and frame agreements
signals.note: Skanska, NCC, Hent, Contiga, Statens vegvesen; nationwide logistics footprint from Kristiansand to Tromsø creates defensible market position.

signals.signal: No shareholder or board information found
signals.note: Ownership structure is the single gating data gap; everything else in the scoring is provisional until it is resolved.
Registry leads convert at 17% (n=6) and the 'open' framing replies best in Norway at 33% — but that base rate is drawn from owner-led SMEs, not group subsidiaries.

risks: Decision-maker is almost certainly a foreign parent/group, not the 61-year-old CEO — outreach to Marthinsen may never reach the shareholder.
Transaction perimeter unclear: is the Mo i Rana EAF mill in or out? Intercompany rebar supply pricing would determine standalone margin and could make the entity unsaleable separately.
Commodity steel price exposure and working-capital swings; the 2025 net loss is unexplained and may be structural rather than one-off.
Customer concentration among a handful of large Norwegian contractors with project-based, cyclical volumes tied to Norwegian construction activity.
Size and sector place it outside every active mandate in the current buyer network; Mergero would be originating for buyers it does not yet have.
Asset-heavy balance sheet with unknown net debt after recent capex — equity value could be materially below any revenue-based intuition.

facts.claim: 7 Steel Service is a total supplier of reinforcement products to the Norwegian market, including cut-and-bend rebar, mesh, roll reinforcement, prefabricated cages and specification/drawing services.
Product categories include rebar (kamstål), reinforcement accessories, technical accessories, formwork and waterproofing.
7 Steel's steel mill in Mo i Rana, Norway supplies the company's rebar, which is distributed via 7 Steel facilities around Norway.
The company claims its rebar is Europe's cleanest with only 388 kg CO2 equivalents per tonne of steel produced.
7 Steel Service Norway AS is certified to NS-EN ISO 14001:2015 and products certified by Kontrollrådet to NS-EN 10080:2005 and NS 3576-3:2012.
The company positions itself as the Nordics' largest manufacturer of reinforcement products.
7 Steel delivers nationwide in Norway with production and warehouses in several locations and sales offices from Kristiansand in the south to Tromsø in the north.
Certificates cover sites in Oslo, Drammen, Kristiansand, Bergen, Ålesund, Trondheim and Tromsø.
The company holds NS-EN ISO 9001:2015 and NS-EN ISO 14001:2015 certificates, ECOproduct, a product certificate for stainless/acid-proof rebar, and is a member of Grønt Punkt Norge.
Richard Buskum is Sales Manager (Salgssjef) for Oslo/Akershus/Østfold/Hedmark/Oppland.
Arild Larsen is Sales Manager and department head in Trondheim.
Stian Pareliussen is Production Manager in Drammen.
Jan Malyszko is Technical Manager (Teknisk sjef).
In May 2023 the Trondheim department hired technical advisor Kinga Walawender (29) for its new factory.
A new, improved EPD was published, giving roughly 40% reduction in climate impact.
Low climate impact is attributed to hydropower, circular Nordic scrap, hot charging, and the steel mill in Mo Industripark.
The company sees CBAM as a strategic confirmation of its 100% scrap-based, hydropower-driven EAF production model.
Production is 100% scrap-based using an electric arc furnace with best available technology and hydropower as primary energy source.
Value-added services include rebar drawing, 3D/BIM modelling, colour marking, bundle sorting by colour, and technical advisory including Bamtec and prefabricated cages.
The company performs mechanical testing of rebar according to NS-EN 15630-1 and NS-EN 15630-2.
Customers can order rebar digitally from IFC/BIM models; standard diameters delivered are 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25 and 32 mm, with Ø40 as a special order.
Special welded mesh (spesialnett) is produced to NS 3576 part 4 and is certified by Kontrollrådet, Class K.
The company supplied reinforcement to NCC's Valle Wood office project in Oslo, whose first phase contract was worth NOK 190 million.
Supplied Skanska's EK3 Farriseidet project in Larvik with a project volume of about 800 tonnes, final delivery autumn 2019.
In January 2020 a new cooperation agreement was signed with Hent AS covering all reinforcement products.
In December 2019 a contract was signed with Contiga for rebar deliveries to all their factories in Norway.
Supplies prefabricated reinforcement solutions to Brødrene Ulveseth in Bergen.
The company supplies its steel to Statens vegvesen's Lepsøyrevet project, part of FV 659 Nordøyvegen.
Strand AS renewed its agreement for all reinforcement solutions with the Bergen department in March 2019.
Asle Nordås is regional manager at the Bergen department.
The company was previously known as Celsa Steel Service and refers to Celsa Steel Service's value chain.
In May 2022 the company confirmed compliance with international sanctions on goods and services from Russia and Belarus.
In March 2018 the company marked 10 years without a lost-time injury.
The Bergen department moved into new premises in October 2017; new premises in Ålesund in July 2017.
Brødrene Ulveseth was the first company to attend a technical day at the Bergen department, focused on BIM solutions.
All rebar delivered is environmentally declared through an underlying LCA analysis, stated at 388 kg CO2/ton.
The company promotes Melt and Pour documentation requirements ahead of new EU steel import rules from 1 October 2026.
Norway will begin applying CBAM from 1 January 2027, while EU importers started paying from 1 January 2026.
Marius Haagensen Bonkerud joined the Oslo department as production planner in December 2019.

7 Steel Service Norway supplies reinforcement steel (kamstål, kamtråd), roll reinforcement (BAMTEC), stainless/acid-proof reinforcement, standard and project-specific reinforcement mesh, prefabricated reinforcement solutions (SWP), and concrete/rebar accessories.
